mcqs.question: What does the term 'amplitude' refer to in a sound wave?

options.A: The maximum displacement of particles from their rest position
options.B: The number of vibrations per second
options.C: The time taken for one complete vibration
options.D: The speed at which the wave travels through the medium

mcqs.answer: The maximum displacement of particles from their rest position
mcqs.explanation: Amplitude is the greatest distance that particles of the medium move from their equilibrium position during a vibration. It is not related to frequency, period, or speed of the wave.

mcqs.question: A tuning fork vibrates 256 times in one second. What is the frequency of the sound produced?
mcqs.explanation: Frequency is the number of vibrations per second and is measured in hertz (Hz). Since the fork makes 256 vibrations each second, its frequency is 256 Hz. The other options represent incorrect multiples or fractions of the correct value.

mcqs.question: A sound wave has a frequency of 250 Hz. What is its time period?
mcqs.explanation: Time period (T) is the reciprocal of frequency (f): T = 1/f. For f = 250 Hz, T = 1/250 = 0.004 seconds. The other options are incorrect reciprocals of different frequencies.

mcqs.question: A drum produces a tone whose time period is 0.002 seconds. What is the frequency of this tone?
mcqs.explanation: Frequency and time period are inversely related: f = 1/T. With T = 0.002 s, f = 1/0.002 = 500 Hz. Option B would correspond to a period of 0.004 s, and the other options are far off.

mcqs.question: Two sounds have the same frequency, but Sound A has a larger amplitude than Sound B. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Sound A will be heard as louder than Sound B
options.B: Both sounds will be equally loud because loudness depends only on frequency
options.C: Sound B will be louder because loudness depends on time period
options.D: Amplitude does not affect loudness; only the medium does

mcqs.answer: Sound A will be heard as louder than Sound B
mcqs.explanation: Loudness is primarily related to the amplitude of the sound wave: larger amplitude means greater energy and a louder perception. Frequency determines pitch, not loudness. Options B, C, and D are misconceptions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between frequency and pitch of a sound?

options.A: Higher frequency corresponds to a higher perceived pitch
options.B: Higher frequency corresponds to a lower perceived pitch
options.C: Pitch is independent of frequency and depends only on amplitude
options.D: Pitch depends on the speed of sound in the medium, not on frequency

mcqs.answer: Higher frequency corresponds to a higher perceived pitch
mcqs.explanation: Pitch is the auditory sensation that allows us to order sounds on a musical scale, and it increases with frequency. Options B, C, and D confuse pitch with other properties.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes amplitude from frequency in a sound wave?

options.A: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of particles, whereas frequency is the number of vibrations per second
options.B: Amplitude is the number of vibrations per second, whereas frequency is the maximum displacement of particles
options.C: Both amplitude and frequency measure the same property of a sound wave
options.D: Amplitude determines the pitch, while frequency determines the loudness

mcqs.answer: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of particles, whereas frequency is the number of vibrations per second
mcqs.explanation: Amplitude relates to the size of particle motion (loudness), while frequency relates to how many cycles occur each second (pitch). Options B, C, and D invert or confuse the definitions.

mcqs.question: The musical note C4 has a frequency of 261.6 Hz. What is the frequency of the note one octave higher (C5)?
mcqs.explanation: An octave higher means the frequency doubles. Doubling 261.6 Hz gives 523.2 Hz. Option B is the original frequency, C is half, and D is two octaves higher (four times).
